question.text: Under SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations 2015, a 'Designated Person' cannot trade in shares during the TRADING WINDOW CLOSURE. The closure typically starts:

answer.text: End of quarter till 48 hours after results announcement

explanation.text: The Logic: Under SEBI's PIT Regulations 2015 framework for listed companies, the trading window for Designated Persons is closed during periods when unpublished price-sensitive information is likely to exist. For quarterly financial results, that period is conventionally treated as starting at the end of the relevant quarter and continuing until at least 48 hours after the results are made public — i.e. once the information has been reasonably disseminated. The Trap: A 1-day pre-results blackout is too short to cover the UPSI period; '2 weeks before AGM' confuses the AGM with the results announcement; 'always open' contradicts the PIT framework's whole purpose. Note: The NISM-Series-XXI-B workbook pages on insider trading (pp. 196-198) cover designated persons, pre-clearance, restricted lists, contra-trade periods and material-financial-relationship disclosures, but do not explicitly state the 'end of quarter until 48 hours after results' trading-window rule. The framing above reflects the general SEBI PIT regime applied to listed entities.
